text:
jordan: Hey team — running into a hang in JupyterLab when my notebook cell calls the Redwood Python SDK. I hit an upstream 502 and the cell never completes. I see a RuntimeError about asyncio.run and then retries seem to spin forever. Not sure if this is an SDK bug or my setup.

mira: Sorry you're hitting that. Can you paste the smallest repro snippet you have + package versions (python, redwood-sdk, httpx)? Also are you using the sync wrapper or the async client?

jordan: Python 3.11, redwood-sdk==0.8.2, httpx==0.24.0, running inside JupyterLab on mac. I'm using the sync helper because I'm calling from cells. Minimal repro below — it hangs on the second call after an intermittent 502 from our proxy: 

```py
from redwood import Client  # sync wrapper
client = Client(api_key="redacted")
# do a call that sometimes 502s
resp = client.generate("hi")
# second call often never returns after transient 502
resp2 = client.generate("still here?")
```

mira: Thanks. Two things to check: 1) sync wrappers that call into asyncio.run will fail inside a running event loop (Jupyter), giving that RuntimeError and sometimes leaving sockets/pools in a bad state so subsequent calls hang. 2) httpx connection pool exhaustion combined with automatic retries can mask the root cause.

alex: Confirming — we shipped a version where the sync shim uses asyncio.run naively which is incompatible with IPython's event loop. That can lead to nested-loop errors and stuck background tasks that keep retrying requests. There's a fix in the SDK (0.9.1) which either uses an explicit async API or applies a nest_asyncio-aware path for notebooks. If you can upgrade, that should help.

mira: Workarounds while you upgrade: either call the async API from the notebook or apply nest_asyncio. Example async usage: 

```py
import asyncio
from redwood import AsyncClient

async def quick():
    async with AsyncClient(api_key="redacted") as c:
        r = await c.generate("hello")
        print(r.text)

await quick()  # works in modern IPython
```

Or (temporary) in a cell at kernel start: 
```py
import nest_asyncio
nest_asyncio.apply()
```

jordan: Noted. Is there anything I should change about httpx limits or retry settings to avoid leaking connections while I test?

mira: Good question — yes. If you keep using the sync path temporarily, reduce concurrency/keepalive and disable aggressive retries to avoid connection pile-up. Example: 

```py
from httpx import Limits, AsyncClient
limits = Limits(max_connections=10, max_keepalive_connections=5)
async with AsyncClient(limits=limits) as client:
    # pass underlying client into redwood AsyncClient if you construct it yourself
    ...

# also set retry policy: retries=1 and add idempotency keys for mutating requests
```

alex: Also note: if you see duplicate charges or duplicated mutating requests during retries, add an idempotency token on the request side. Retries + partial failures are the common root for billing/dup issues.

jordan: I upgraded to 0.9.1 and switched to AsyncClient with the limits change. After a few flaky 502s the notebook no longer hangs and subsequent calls recover. No duplication either with the idempotency header set. Thanks! :tada:

mira: Awesome — glad that worked. We'll mark this resolved. If you hit it again, please paste the full stack trace and we can dig deeper.

support-bot: Ticket #12345 updated: status -> resolved (jordan)

ops-bot: Docs: https://docs.redwood.com/sdk/python#async-notebooks — recommends async usage in notebooks and nest_asyncio workaround

alex: Follow-up: we'll add a small FAQ entry about notebooks and the sync shim in the next patch release to avoid future surprises.

jordan: Thanks everyone. Closing from my side.
